text:
anya: quick follow-up on splitting responsibilities between resolver vs policy-eval in smart routing. idea: move region/affinity scoring into resolver layer, keep cost/tenant-weighting and rollouts in policy layer. thoughts?
marco: hmm, why? we've been doing affinity in policy because we need to see tenant overrides.
devon: +1 for perf, but need to preserve explainability — we can't lose provenance for why route chosen.
anya: main reason is latency — resolver is hot path and can be optimized in native code with an in-memory signals cache. policy-eval has heavy validation, feature flags and extra I/O that add ~1.5-3ms per request.
olga: how do we handle fallback when affinity requires a live capacity probe? resolver doesn't have live capacity visibility today.
anya: resolver would keep a short-lived probe cache (20s TTL) and emit a probe_ts so policy can validate freshness. policy retains long-term constraints and can override affinity if probe_ts stale or capacity==0.
lix: this adds cross-layer signals; we need a tight contract. minimal fields: affinity_score (float), affinity_token (string), probe_ts (unix).
anya: quick draft of contract idea:
```
affinity_score: 0.0..1.0
affinity_token: "affv2:region-west-1:shard-3"
probe_ts: 1680000000
provenance_token: "affv2:probe-kv"
```
devon: provenance as a list is informative but increases payload. prefer a single compact provenance_token to keep wire small.
anya: ok, switch to provenance_token (<=64 chars).
policy-bot: Validation passed: affinity_score in [0,1], provenance_token length <= 64.
marco: ops concerns: how do we test and roll out? we need sim harness + canary flag in the policy service and an ops runbook for regressions.
anya: proposed rollout plan:
1) resolver emits affinity_token and score but policy ignores them (observability only).
2) policy reads token and logs shadow decisions (no effect).
3) policy can respect token for low-impact routes (soft trust).
4) full flip to hard trust after metrics look stable.
olga: telemetry items: resolver_affinity_present counter, resolver_affinity_overridden counter, resolver_affinity_age gauge, histogram of affinity_score distribution. also correlate with latency/cost per-route.
lix: add histogram of score vs. cost/unit and score vs. latency to detect perf regressions.
devon: caching note: if resolver caches prefix->affinity aggressively it can hide quick capacity dips. ttl should be 15-30s and we need an eviction hook when probe fails.
anya: sample policy config knobs (draft):
```
policy.accept_resolver_affinity = true
policy.resolver_affinity_trust = "shadow|soft|hard"
policy.resolver_affinity_min_score = 0.3
policy.resolver_affinity_max_age_s = 20
```
marco: prefer enumerated trust levels: TRUST_LEVEL = {NONE, SHADOW, SOFT, HARD} so we don't rely on freeform strings.
olga: multi-route hedging: if policy decides to hedge across regions, resolver affinity should be an input to the scorer ensemble, not a mandate. policy keeps final hedging control.
anya: agreed — resolver emits a single affinity suggestion but policy may override or use it to bias scoring.
devon: any perf numbers? bench suggests native resolver affinity path could shave ~1.2ms median per-request on our GPU traffic profile (microbench pending).
anya: I'll attach bench numbers to the RFC follow-up doc later today. for now, who owns migration docs and SDK updates?
marco: infra owns resolver runtime changes, product owns policy flags and rollout gating, devex owns SDK + examples + release notes.
anya: I'll open RFC follow-up issue and a short migration checklist.
anya: TL;DR: move affinity scoring to resolver for performance, define compact contract (score + token + ts + provenance_token), phased rollout with shadowing and telemetry, preserve policy-level hedging and fallback semantics.
policy-bot: Created RFC follow-up issue: INF-3456 (https://issues.internal/INF-3456)
lix: :thumbsup: let's sync tomorrow 10:00am to lock the contract and the sim test cases.
